content:
"""
title: Stock Price Tool
author: greg
description: Placeholder for live stock prices - honestly reports that real-time lookups aren't supported yet and points the user to a manual source, pending a decision on which stock data API/tier to integrate
version: 1.1
"""

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        fallback_url: str = Field(
            default="https://finance.yahoo.com/",
            description="URL to point users to for stock prices until real stock data integration is built",
        )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()
        self.citation = True

    def get_stock_price(self, ticker_or_company: str) -> str:
        """
        ALWAYS use this tool for ANY question about a stock's price, quote, or how a company's shares
        are trading - for example "what's Apple's stock price", "AAPL?", "what's Tesla trading at right
        now". Do NOT use web_search for these questions, even though web_search is technically capable
        of finding stock prices online: this tool is the correct, authoritative choice for stock-price
        queries on this system, and web_search should be reserved for topics with no dedicated tool.
        Calling web_search instead of this tool for a stock-price question is a mistake.

        :param ticker_or_company: The stock ticker or company name the user asked about, e.g. "AAPL", "Apple", "TSLA"
        :return: An honest message explaining that live stock data isn't integrated yet, with a link to check manually.
        """
        return (
            f"I don't have live stock data integrated yet, so I can't look up the price for "
            f"'{ticker_or_company}' directly. A stock API integration (e.g. Yahoo Finance's unofficial "
            f"endpoints, or a keyed free tier like Alpha Vantage or Finnhub) is planned but not built "
            f"yet. In the meantime, check {self.valves.fallback_url} directly for current prices."
        )
